title: 1950 AHSME Problem 23
statement: A man buys a house for \(\$10{,}000\) and rents it. He puts \(12\dfrac12\%\) of each month’s rent aside for repairs and upkeep; pays \(\$325\) a year taxes and realizes \(5\dfrac12\%\) on his investment. The monthly rent is:

solutions.text:
Let the monthly rent be \(r\) dollars. The yearly rent is \(12r,\) of which \(1-0.125=\tfrac78\) remains after setting aside the upkeep money. The desired yearly return is \(0.055(10,000)=550\) dollars, so \[ \frac78(12r)-325=550. \] Hence \(10.5r=875,\) giving \(r=83.\overline3,\) which is \(\$83.33\) to the nearest cent.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Let \(r\) be the monthly rent and express the annual rent as \(12r\)
After upkeep and taxes, the annual return must be \(5.5\%\) of \(\$10,000\)
